newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - CFDs, naphtha gain but not others.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - CFDs, naphtha gain but not others.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Wednesday.
Heavy fuel lost about $1 and gasoline slipped 50 cents to $1, but naphtha heeded crude futures' rise and put on $1-2 a tonne.
Brent crude CFDs perked up several cents supported by stronger screen numbers and six or seven wet deals which thinned out some previously overhanging barrels.
Brent CFDs edged higher, bar stagnant June 11-13, dealers said.

No CFDs were thought traded, but June 16-20 numbers were hiked up to -64/65 cents against August Brent from -77 cents and June 23-27 gained to -54 cents from -67. June 30-July 4 was subjected to less talk, but prices were also stronger at -47/48 cents against August Brent compared with -59 cents on Tuesday.
Heavy fuel saw June trading at $84 and $84.25, up to $1 weaker than Tuesday's numbers. Dealers said there was some aggresive offers, although few players were prepared to pick up.
June was heard offered late in the day at $84.50 with July 50 cents contangoed and August about $1 stronger than July.
Gasoline swaps were actively traded on July with $182.25, $182.50, $182.75 and $183 all done. June was valued at about $187, off $1 and August traded at $183.75.
On the wet side the U.S arb was shut, but tightness in the ARA barge market gave some support. A refiner paid $195.25 fob AR for 13-25 June dates.

Naphtha climbed nearly $2, backed by firmer screen crude and by a wet cargo deal at $186.75 cif Rotterdam for an Alexandria cargo. June swap business was very thin, but July was done at $179 and a touch below.
